relations.subject: Colin Mackenzie
relations.evidence: In his youth he had an interest in mathematics possibly fostered by his schoolmaster, a freemason, Alexander Anderson.

relations.subject: Colin Mackenzie
relations.evidence: Colin Mackenzie was appointed Surveyor General of Madras Presidency in 1810 but these posts were abolished in 1815.

relations.subject: Colin Mackenzie
relations.evidence: On 26 May 1815 he was appointed Surveyor General of India with his headquarters at Fort William in Calcutta

relations.subject: Colin Mackenzie
relations.evidence: One of his chief interpreters was a Niyogi Brahmin named Kavelli Venkata Boria... who Mackenzie first met in 1796... Boria died in 1803

relations.subject: Colin Mackenzie
relations.evidence: Boria died in 1803 and Mackenzie took in his brother Venkata Lechmiah... When Mackenzie moved from Madras to Calcutta, Lechmiah was retained.

relations.subject: Colin Mackenzie
relations.evidence: Another of Mackenzie's assistant was Dhurmiah... a Jain pandit (scholar) from Maleyur... Dhurmiah provided Mackenzie with Jain insights into the history of India

relations.subject: Sir Alexander Johnston
relations.object: Royal Asiatic Society of Great Britain and Ireland
relations.evidence: their son Alexander Johnston later became a judge in Sri Lanka, founded the Royal Asiatic Society of Great Britain and Ireland

relations.subject: Venkata Lechmiah
relations.evidence: After Mackenzie's death, Lechmiah continued to help Horace Hayman Wilson in cataloguing the collections.

relations.subject: Venkata Lechmiah
relations.evidence: in 1833, Lechmiah founded a parallel Madras Hindu Literary Society as a means of continuing his work.
